cards.explanation: The answer is to learn them and observe them carefully. Moses says, “Learn them and observe them carefully.” Hearing is only the first step. He wants these words to sink in and then show up in how Israel lives. Reading a cookie recipe has never put one cookie in anybody's mouth, friends.

The answer is False. Moses says God “…did not make this covenant with our fathers, but with all of us who are alive here today.” The people in front of him were the ones God made it with at Horeb. It was their covenant, not an old family story.

The answer is that they were afraid of the fire. Moses says they were afraid of the fire and wouldn't go up the mountain. That's the reason the text gives, plain and simple. Fire on a mountain is no small thing, and I think I'd have stayed at the bottom too. My own hat has a hard enough time near a hot oven.

The answer is “between.” Moses says he was standing between the LORD and the people to declare to them the word of the LORD. He says the people were afraid of the fire and would not go up the mountain (Deuteronomy 5:5). So he stood in the middle and carried God's words to them. I'd call that a job with a view, and I think it took some nerve.

The answer is that they must have no other gods before Him. God says, “You shall have no other gods before Me.” Right before it, He reminds them He brought them out of Egypt, out of the house of slavery (Deuteronomy 5:6). So He doesn't open with a rule, He opens with “Remember who just carried you out of there.” I've been rescued from a place myself, friends, and you don't forget who came and got you.

The answer is True. God says, “You shall not bow down to them or worship them…” Right before that He forbids making an idol of anything in the heavens, on the earth or in the waters. So it's no making them and no bowing to them.

The answer is “jealous.” God says, “…I, the LORD your God, am a jealous God…” That's the reason He gives for not bowing down to idols. He's not telling Israel to stay far away, either. He says it plainly about Himself, and I'd take Him at His word.

The answer is to a thousand generations. God says He shows “…loving devotion to a thousand generations of those who love Me and keep My commandments.” That's a big number. It would take a lot of family reunions to count that far. A thousand generations is a very long reach for His loving devotion.
The answer is True. God says, “…the LORD will not leave anyone unpunished who takes His name in vain.” It comes right with the command. His name is not something to throw around lightly, friends.

The answer is six and seventh. God says, “Six days you shall labor and do all your work…” Then comes the rest. God says, “…the seventh day is a Sabbath to the LORD your God…” The week ends with a day set apart for the LORD.

The answer is everyone, including servants and livestock. God lists them: “…neither you, nor your son or daughter, nor your manservant or maidservant, nor your ox or donkey or any of your livestock, nor the foreigner within your gates…” Everybody on the property gets the day. He even says why the servants are included: “…so that your manservant and maidservant may rest as you do.” The rest is for the whole household.

The answer is that they were slaves and He brought them out. God says, “Remember that you were a slave in the land of Egypt, and that the LORD your God brought you out of there with a mighty hand and an outstretched arm.” Then He adds, “That is why the LORD your God has commanded you to keep the Sabbath day.” So the Sabbath is tied to the rescue. Rest is part of remembering who pulled them out.

The answer is “days.” God says, “…so that your days may be long and that it may go well with you in the land that the LORD your God is giving you.” This is the command that comes with a promise attached. Honoring father and mother is tied to long days and things going well.
The answer is “You shall not steal.” That's what God says. Nobody takes what belongs to someone else. It's a short command, and it needs no footnotes. If it's not yours, it's not yours, friends.

The answer is that they must not bear false witness against a neighbor. God says, “You shall not bear false witness against your neighbor.” It's about what Israel says about a neighbor. A false word about someone is something God forbids. Keep your words honest, friends.

The answer is False. The wife is only the first thing on the list. God goes on: “You shall not covet your neighbor’s house or field, or his manservant or maidservant, or his ox or donkey, or anything that belongs to your neighbor.” That last phrase covers everything else.

The answer is nothing more at all. Moses says, “He added nothing more.” God spoke these commandments out of the fire, the cloud and the deep darkness, and then He stopped. Then He wrote them on two tablets of stone and gave them to Moses.
The answer is “stone.” Moses says God wrote the commandments on two tablets of stone and gave them to him. They weren't only spoken out of the fire. They were written down and handed to Moses.

The answer is True. Moses reminds them they said, “Today we have seen that a man can live even if God speaks with him.” They had heard God's voice out of the fire, and they were still standing. That's what they told him that day.

The answer is that the great fire will consume them. They say, “…this great fire will consume us, and we will die, if we hear the voice of the LORD our God any longer.” They'd just seen a man can live, but they still feared the fire. That's the worry they bring to Moses. I think it's the fire that has them shaking.

The answer is “obey.” They say, “we will listen and obey.” First they ask Moses to go near and hear everything the LORD says, then tell them. Listening comes with obeying. It's a good promise, friends.

The answer is False. God tells Moses, “I have heard the words that these people have spoken to you. They have done well in all that they have spoken.” He's not scolding them for what they said. He says they did well.

The answer is so it would go well with them and their children. God says, “…so that it might be well with them and with their children forever.” His wish is tied to their good, and to their children's good too. It's a wish with the family in view.

The answer is False. God tells Moses to tell the people, “Return to your tents.” Then He tells Moses, “But you stand here with Me…” He's there so God can speak all the commandments, statutes and ordinances to him. Moses is being kept close, friends.
The answer is none to the right or left. Moses says, “you are not to turn aside to the right or to the left.” He doesn't leave a gap on either side. It's a straight road, friends. Stay on it.

The answer is True. Moses says, “You must walk in all the ways that the LORD your God has commanded you, so that you may live and prosper and prolong your days in the land that you will possess.” That's the reason he gives for walking in all God's ways.
